title: Unity 6
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Unity 6.3 LTS supported until December 2027 and Unity 6.0 LTS through October 2026, each with an extra year for Enterprise and Industry; Unity 6.2 named as a Supported Update release; no runtime fee for games made with Unity 6.

title: Pricing updates
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Runtime Fee cancelled on 12 September 2024; Unity Personal for up to $200,000 in revenue and funding from 17 October 2024 with Unity 6; splash screen optional with Unity 6 Personal; Pro required above $200,000 from 1 January 2025; price rise for Pro and Enterprise from 12 January 2026 (price figures not used).

title: Fixed updates
supports: Opened with WebFetch (redirected from docs.unity3d.com; the current manual is Unity 6.6, 6000.6). Fixed timestep set in Time.fixedDeltaTime or the Time window; physics runs at a fixed interval; with a 0.02 timestep at about 128 fps each frame has one fixed update or none; with 0.01 at about 38 to 40 fps there are two or three per frame; FixedUpdate is for physics code such as forces; a lower timestep costs more CPU; a maximum timestep limits catch-up.

title: Event function execution order
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Physics step runs directly after FixedUpdate in the default simulation mode; WaitForFixedUpdate resumes at the end of the fixed step and WaitForEndOfFrame at the end of the frame; order of the same event across GameObjects is not guaranteed, so use Script Execution Order; the Built-in Render Pipeline is deprecated and supported through Unity 6.7 LTS.

title: Event functions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. All Awake calls finish before the first Start; Update runs before rendering and animation; FixedUpdate runs just before each physics update and gives more accurate physics; LateUpdate runs after all Update and FixedUpdate calls and animation, for cameras; OnMouse callbacks need the legacy Input Manager, which is no longer recommended; OnGUI is legacy.

title: Rigidbody interpolation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Jitter appears when physics updates run slower than the frame rate, most visibly on a body the camera follows; Interpolate (one physics step of lag) and Extrapolate (can overshoot); default None; use only if jitter shows; with either on, direct transform changes need Physics.SyncTransforms.

title: Continuous collision detection
supports: Opened with WebFetch. CCD predicts collisions between physics steps as a safety net for colliders passing through each other; more accurate but costlier than discrete; Continuous, Continuous Dynamic (sweep-based) and Continuous Speculative; supports Box, Sphere and Capsule colliders; not always physically accurate.

title: ScriptableObject
supports: Opened with WebFetch. ScriptableObjects are data assets, not components; share data between objects to avoid copies; CreateAssetMenu attribute; script edits in Edit mode need EditorUtility.SetDirty to persist; in a standalone Player saved data can only be read from the assets.

title: Application.persistentDataPath
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A directory for data kept between runs; example paths per platform; desktop paths include company and product name, so renaming moves saves; mobile path includes a GUID from the bundle identifier, so keep it the same across updates; files on iOS and Android are not erased by app updates; the page lists 6000.3 as the LTS.

title: Smart merge
supports: Opened with WebFetch. UnityYAMLMerge merges .unity, .prefab and .meta files semantically; needed when two people change the same scene or prefab in parallel; Git configuration through a merge tool entry; tool locations per operating system; merge rules file.

title: Test Framework (core package)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Test framework for running Edit mode and Play mode tests; core packages are fixed to a single version matching the Editor version.

title: Input System (package)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A more extensible and customisable alternative to the classic UnityEngine.Input system; package version 1.20.1 released for Unity 6000.6.

title: Idle and physics processing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Stable docs are for Godot 4.7; _process runs every drawn frame and varies with frame rate; _physics_process runs before each physics step, 60 times per second by default (Project Settings, Physics, Common, Physics Fps); multiply by delta; physics-body movement goes in _physics_process.

title: License
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Godot is MIT licensed; you own your games; shipping the engine with a game counts as redistribution and needs the copyright notice and licence text, for example in the credits; third-party parts listed in COPYRIGHT.txt.

title: Actor ticking in Unreal Engine
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Page is for Unreal Engine 5.8; tick groups TG_PrePhysics, TG_DuringPhysics, TG_PostPhysics and TG_PostUpdateWork in order; bCanEverTick in the constructor; SetActorTickEnabled at runtime; tick prerequisites; actors tick once per frame unless a minimum interval is set.

title: Steam Direct fee
supports: Opened with WebFetch. $100 USD (or equivalent) per new app, not refundable but recoupable once the product reaches $1,000 adjusted gross revenue; paid during onboarding by a user with Admin permissions.

title: Review process
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Store page and build are each reviewed before release, typically in 3 to 5 business days; submit at least 7 business days ahead; screenshots must show gameplay; the build must start on every listed operating system and include every listed feature; in-game transactions must use Steam Wallet; approval is a one-time step.

title: Coming Soon
supports: Opened with WebFetch. New products need a Coming Soon page live at least two weeks before release; review request at least 7 business days before the page should go live; wishlisters get an email at release; the page activates the Community Hub.

title: Content Survey
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The survey is completed before store page and build review; General Content answers generate regional ratings shown on the store page; official ratings can be entered separately; mature content disclosure; Generative AI section covers pre-generated and live-generated content, with guardrails needed for live generation; locked answers change only through Steam Support.

title: Uploading to Steam
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SteamPipe ContentBuilder and steamcmd run_app_build; Preview builds output only logs; a dedicated build account with Edit App Metadata and Publish App Changes To Steam permissions; SetLive can set a beta branch live but the default branch can't be set live automatically; setting a build live on a released app needs a phone number or the Steam Mobile App, and a 3-day wait after security changes.

title: Steam Cloud
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Steam Cloud API versus Steam Auto-Cloud; per-user, per-game byte and file quotas you set; 100 MB per write call; smaller files work better; split state by how often it changes; avoid machine-specific settings; make paths unique per user; default cross-platform setting recommended; test with developer-only cloud support.

title: Participating storefronts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Storefronts listed: Epic Games, Facebook Gaming, Fortnite, Google Play, Luna, Meta Horizon, Microsoft, Nintendo, One Store, Pico, Sony PlayStation and YouTube Playables; regional ratings shown include ACB, ClassInd, ESRB, PEGI, USK and others. Steam and the Apple App Store are not listed.

title: Content ratings
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Every app needs an IARC content rating from the Play Console questionnaire; apps without one are removed; retake the questionnaire when content or features change the answers; misrepresentation can mean removal or suspension; ads must not be much more mature than the app; appeals go to the rating authority.

title: What do the labels mean?
supports: Opened with WebFetch. PEGI 3, 7, 12, 16 and 18 and content descriptors; the In-game purchases descriptor and the paid random items notice; since June 2026, games with paid random items are rated PEGI 16 (PEGI 18 for social casino), time-limited offers PEGI 12 (PEGI 7 with spending off by default in parental controls), pressure-to-play rewards PEGI 7 or 12, unrestricted communication PEGI 18; NFTs required to play PEGI 18.

title: Ratings guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Categories E, E10+, T, M, AO and RP; content descriptors; interactive elements including In-Game Purchases and In-Game Purchases (Includes Random Items), which covers purchases with real money or with in-game currency bought with real money; interactive elements don't affect the rating.

title: App Review Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch (Last Updated 16 October 2026). 3.1.1: apps offering loot boxes or other paid randomised virtual items must disclose the odds of each item type before purchase.

title: Payments (Monetization and Ads policy)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Section 7: apps and games offering randomised virtual items from a purchase, including loot boxes, must clearly disclose the odds in advance of and close to the purchase; Google Play billing for digital goods with listed exceptions; virtual currency only usable in the app or game it was bought for.

title: Government response to the call for evidence on loot boxes in video games
publisher: UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 18 July 2022; no change to the Gambling Act 2005 at that time; industry-led protections preferred, including that under-18s should not buy loot boxes unless a parent or guardian enables it, better age assurance, spending controls and transparent information; research found an association with harms but no proven causal link.

title: MEPs call for better protection of gamers and their data
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Report adopted 18 January 2023 by 577 votes to 56 with 15 abstentions; calls for parental tools, clearer labelling of in-game purchase policies possibly modelled on PEGI (used in 38 countries), protection of minors from prompts to make in-game purchases, and design that avoids feeding addiction.

title: Fortnite Video Game Maker Epic Games to Pay More Than Half a Billion Dollars over FTC Allegations
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 19 December 2022: $275 million COPPA penalty and $245 million refunds; alleged dark patterns in button layout causing unwanted purchases; children could buy currency without consent until 2018; voice and text chat on by default; order bars charging without affirmative consent.
